LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard metadata and sources for the `superseedr-bin` package. The `source` array entries fetch a README and LICENSE file directly from the project's GitHub release tag via HTTPS, using a predictable URL based on `_gitversion`. Additionally, a prebuilt `.deb` file is downloaded for x86_64 from the official GitHub releases page. All sources originate from the declared upstream repository (`https://github.com/Jagalite/superseedr`), which is consistent with expected packaging behavior.

No top-level command substitutions, dynamic sourcing, or execution of external code occurs during the sourcing of this PKGBUILD. The variables are statically defined or derived from other static variables (e.g., `_ghurl`, `_ghurlraw`). The `pkgver()` function is not present, so version computation does not involve any runtime logic that could hide malicious behavior. As such, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only result in downloading the specified sources — no code execution occurs at this stage.

Although the `.deb` file is extracted later in the `package()` function (which is not executed under `--noprepare`), the extraction itself during this phase is not performed. The use of `sha256sums` with valid checksums — even if they were set to 'SKIP' — would not affect the safety of this step, as source verification is separate from execution risk. There is no evidence of obfuscated commands, data exfiltration, or remote code execution triggered during PKGBUILD sourcing or source download.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No dangerous operations during source fetch and PKGBUILD sourcing
</summary>
</security_assessment>
